concepts.preferred_label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
concepts.why: The patient has a history of NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and laboratory tests show elevated brain natriuretic peptide and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction.
The patient's ECG shows sinus tachycardia and alternating QRS complex morphologies, which are characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome.
The patient has a history of heart failure and presents with mild wheezing and elevated brain natriuretic peptide, which may indicate pulmonary hypertension.

The patient has a history of polysubstance abuse and presents with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and global hypokinesis, which are characteristic of cardiomyopathy due to substance abuse.
The patient presents with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which may indicate nephrotic syndrome.
The patient presents with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema and mild wheezing, which may indicate constrictive pericarditis.
The patient presents with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema and mild wheezing, which may indicate tricuspid regurgitation.
The patient has a history of heart failure and presents with mild wheezing and elevated brain natriuretic peptide, which may indicate cor pulmonale.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presents with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and global hypokinesis, which are characteristic of hypertensive heart disease.
The patient presents with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, global hypokinesis, and elevated brain natriuretic peptide, which may indicate cardiac amyloidosis.
Elevated troponin level indicates myocardial injury, which is a key feature of acute coronary syndrome.

rationales.F01: Bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema is consistent with right-sided heart failure, which is often seen in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
rationales.F02: The absence of chest pain, shortness of breath, or dyspnea on exertion makes acute coronary syndrome less likely.
rationales.F04: Mild wheezing could be indicative of pulmonary hypertension, which is often seen in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
rationales.F06: A left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 25% is diagnostic of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
rationales.F07: Global hypokinesis is consistent with cardiomyopathy due to substance abuse.
rationales.F09: Alternating QRS complex morphologies are diagnostic of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.
rationales.F10: Elevated troponin levels are consistent with myocardial injury, which is often seen in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and acute coronary syndrome.
rationales.F11: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide levels are diagnostic of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
rationales.F12: NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is consistent with advanced heart failure.
